toc.title: Changing the Sprint Backlog Without Endangering the Sprint Goal (SF 4.4)
Why the Sprint Goal Does Not Change (SF 4.7)
How the Sprint Backlog Is Used
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1The Sprint Backlog (SF 4.1)

"The Sprint Backlog is composed of the Sprint Goal (why), the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what), as well as an actionable plan for delivering the Increment (how)."

1.1 Purpose and attributes (list at least three)

Attribute Guide wording
A plan by and for the Developers "The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers"
Highly visible, real-time "A highly visible, real-time picture of the work that the Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint in order to achieve the Sprint Goal"
Updated throughout the Sprint "The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned"
Enough detail "It should have enough detail that they can inspect their progress in the Daily Scrum"
Three parts Sprint Goal (why) + selected items (what) + plan (how)
Made in Sprint Planning The Sprint Goal, the selected items and the plan "are together referred to as the Sprint Backlog"
Commitment The Sprint Goal

Purpose: to make the plan for the Sprint transparent and to give the Developers the basis for inspecting progress and adapting each day.

Old wording

The 2017 Guide called the Sprint Backlog "a forecast by the Development Team about what functionality will be in the next Increment and the work needed to deliver that functionality". It also said the Sprint Backlog "includes at least one high priority process improvement identified in the previous Retrospective meeting". The 2020 Guide calls it a plan by and for the Developers, and says Retrospective improvements "may even be added" to it.

2The Sprint Goal (SF 4.6)

"The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint. Although the Sprint Goal is a commitment by the Developers, it provides flexibility in terms of the exact work needed to achieve it. The Sprint Goal also creates coherence and focus, encouraging the Scrum Team to work together rather than on separate initiatives."

Fact Guide wording
When it is created "During the Sprint Planning event and then added to the Sprint Backlog"; it must be finalized before the end of Planning
Who creates it The whole Scrum Team: the Product Owner proposes the value, the Scrum Team defines the goal
During the Sprint "As the Developers work during the Sprint, they keep the Sprint Goal in mind"
If the work differs from expectations "They collaborate with the Product Owner to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal"
Cancelling A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, only by the Product Owner
Sprint Goal Product Goal
Scope One Sprint The long-term objective
Artifact Sprint Backlog Product Backlog
Created In Sprint Planning Developed by the Product Owner
Commitment of The Developers (as the Scrum Team's goal for the Sprint) The Scrum Team
Relation Each Sprint Goal moves the team toward the Product Goal Target for all Sprints

3Changing the Sprint Backlog Without Endangering the Sprint Goal (SF 4.4)

The rule: "No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal", while "scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned".

May change (the plan and the scope) May not change
The plan: the Developers update tasks and the order of work, daily and at any time The Sprint Goal is not changed or put at risk
Which items serve the goal: the Developers and the Product Owner negotiate scope, for example replacing an item by a smaller one, splitting an item, or dropping a lower-priority item Beyond the Guideexamples Quality: "Quality does not decrease"; the Definition of Done stays
Detail: the Sprint Backlog "is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned" The Sprint length: Sprints are of fixed length
New findings: tasks discovered during the work are added to the plan Who decides how: the Developers, at their sole discretion
Improvements from the Retrospective may enter the next Sprint Backlog Unrelated work is not added in a way that endangers the goal

3.1 Who may change the Sprint Backlog?

  • The Developers own the Sprint Backlog and update it.
  • The Product Owner does not add items directly: scope is negotiated with the Developers.
  • Stakeholders and managers do not change it. They influence the Product Backlog through the Product Owner.

4Why the Sprint Goal Does Not Change (SF 4.7)Beyond the Guide

The Guide gives the rule and the nature of the goal (a commitment that gives coherence and focus). The reasons follow:

Reason Explanation
It is a commitment The Developers commit to the Sprint Goal; changing it would make the commitment meaningless
Focus and coherence A stable goal keeps the whole team working together rather than on separate initiatives
A stable target for inspection The Daily Scrum and the Sprint Review inspect progress toward a known goal
Predictability and trust Stakeholders can rely on what the Sprint is for
Flexibility sits in the scope The goal is fixed so that the scope can flex without losing direction
The proper response to a changed world is cancelling If the goal becomes obsolete, the Product Owner may cancel the Sprint and the team plans a new one, rather than quietly changing the goal
Exam angle

the goal is fixed and the scope is flexible. When something changes mid-Sprint, the best answer negotiates scope with the Product Owner without endangering the Sprint Goal. If the goal itself is obsolete, only the Product Owner can cancel the Sprint. Options that change the Sprint Goal, add unrelated work or extend the Sprint are wrong.

5How the Sprint Backlog Is Used

Event Use of the Sprint Backlog
Sprint Planning Created: Sprint Goal, selected items, plan
Daily Scrum Inspected and adapted: "enough detail that they can inspect their progress"
During the Sprint Updated as the Developers learn
Sprint Review The Increment is shown; the Sprint Goal and the Sprint Backlog explain what the Sprint aimed to do
Sprint Retrospective The most impactful improvements may be added to the next Sprint Backlog

6Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. Sprint Backlog = Sprint Goal + selected items + plan. Not only a task list.
  2. It belongs to the Developers. They update it. The Product Owner and managers do not assign or add tasks.
  3. It is updated throughout the Sprint, not frozen after Planning.
  4. The Sprint Goal is one objective, created in Planning and finalized before it ends.
  5. The goal is fixed; scope is negotiable between the Developers and the Product Owner.
  6. Quality does not decrease to protect the goal or the scope.
  7. An obsolete Sprint Goal means the Product Owner may cancel the Sprint. Being behind is not obsolescence.
  8. Sprint Goal is the commitment of the Sprint Backlog, not of the Product Backlog.
  9. The Sprint Goal is not a list of items. One missed item does not automatically mean the goal is missed.
  10. Old wording "Forecast" and the required process improvement are 2017 terms; the 2020 Sprint Backlog is a plan.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1Midway through the Sprint, a manager asks the Product Owner to add a new, unrelated item to the Sprint Backlog. What should happen?

  • AThe Product Owner adds it to the Sprint Backlog without telling the Developers
  • BThe Product Owner adds it to the Product Backlog, and negotiates with the Developers if it must enter this Sprint without endangering the Sprint Goal
  • CThe manager adds it to the Sprint Backlog
  • DThe Scrum Master adds it to the Sprint Backlog
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Sprint Backlog is the Developers' plan, and scope may be clarified and renegotiated between the Developers and the Product Owner as long as the Sprint Goal is not endangered. The Product Backlog is where new work goes. Others cannot add items to the Sprint Backlog.

S2The Developers discover that a smaller version of one item would achieve the Sprint Goal and leave room for another important item. May they change the Sprint Backlog?

  • ANo: the Sprint Backlog is fixed after Sprint Planning, and any change needs the approval of the Scrum Master and the Product Owner together
  • BOnly the Scrum Master may change it, because the Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum process
  • COnly if the Sprint is cancelled and a new Sprint Planning is held for the changed Sprint Backlog
  • DYes, with the Product Owner, because the Sprint Backlog is updated all Sprint long and scope may be renegotiated
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned, and scope may be negotiated with the Product Owner as long as the Sprint Goal is not affected. Replacing an item with a smaller one that serves the same goal is typical.

S3A stakeholder wants to change the Sprint Goal on day four to a new priority, although the current goal is still valuable. What is the best answer?

  • AThe Sprint Goal does not change in the Sprint; the new priority goes to the Product Backlog, and only the Product Owner may cancel
  • BChange it, because the stakeholders pay for the product and are the ones who finally decide what the Sprint Goal should be
  • CLet the Developers change it, since they know best which goal they can reach before the Sprint ends
  • DExtend the Sprint so that both the old and the new goal can be reached before the Sprint Review
Show the answer

Answer: A. No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal. The new priority is a Product Backlog matter, decided by the Product Owner. A Sprint can be cancelled only if its Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, and only by the Product Owner.

S4Who owns the Sprint Backlog?

  • AThe Product Owner
  • BThe Scrum Master
  • CThe Developers
  • DThe stakeholders
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers. They update it throughout the Sprint, and use it to inspect progress in the Daily Scrum.

S5The team treats the Sprint Goal as a list of items, and when one item fails it declares the Sprint a failure. What does the Guide suggest?

  • AThe Sprint Goal is the single objective of the Sprint and leaves flexibility in the work, so items may be adjusted
  • BAll items must be completed, otherwise the Sprint has failed and the team must explain it to the stakeholders at the Sprint Review
  • CThe Sprint Goal is optional, so one missed item has no effect on whether the Sprint succeeded
  • DThe Product Owner decides whether the Sprint succeeded, based on how many items were completed
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint, a commitment that provides flexibility in the exact work needed to achieve it. The Developers and the Product Owner negotiate scope without affecting the goal.

S6The Sprint Backlog was created at Sprint Planning and is never updated again. What is wrong?

  • ANothing is wrong: the Sprint Backlog is a fixed contract that must not change once Sprint Planning is over
  • BThe Product Owner should update it every day, because the Product Owner is accountable for the Sprint's progress
  • CIt is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned, and the Developers use it in the Daily Scrum
  • DIt should be replaced by the Product Backlog, which already shows the order of all the work of the team
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work and is updated throughout the Sprint. A frozen plan loses its transparency.

S7Which statement about the Sprint Goal and the Sprint Backlog is correct?

  • AThe Sprint Goal is created before the Sprint Planning by the Product Owner alone
  • BThe Sprint Goal is the commitment of the Product Backlog
  • CThe Sprint Goal is created after the Sprint
  • DThe Sprint Goal is created during Sprint Planning and then added to the Sprint Backlog, where it is the commitment
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Sprint Goal is created during the Sprint Planning event and then added to the Sprint Backlog, and it is the commitment for the Sprint Backlog.

S8What is the difference between the Sprint Goal and the Product Goal?

  • AThey are the same, because the Sprint Goal is only a shorter name for the goal of the whole product
  • BThe Sprint Goal is the single objective of one Sprint; the Product Goal is the long-term objective in the Product Backlog
  • CThe Product Goal is created by the Developers in Sprint Planning, while the Product Owner creates the Sprint Goal before the Sprint Planning starts
  • DThe Sprint Goal lasts for the whole life of the product, while the Product Goal changes in every Sprint
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Product Goal describes a future state of the product and is in the Product Backlog; the Sprint Goal is the objective of one Sprint and is in the Sprint Backlog. Each Sprint Goal moves the team toward the Product Goal.

S9At the Retrospective the team identified an improvement that would increase quality. How can it enter the next Sprint?

  • AThe most impactful improvements may be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint
  • BImprovements may never enter the Sprint Backlog
  • COnly the Product Owner may add improvements
  • DImprovements wait for the next Retrospective
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Guide says the most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible and may even be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint.

7.2 Recall Q&As

R1What is the Sprint Backlog composed of?

Show the answer

The Sprint Goal (why), the Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what), and an actionable plan for delivering the Increment (how).

R2Whose plan is it?

Show the answer

A plan by and for the Developers.

R3What picture does the Sprint Backlog give?

Show the answer

A highly visible, real-time picture of the work the Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint.

R4How often is it updated?

Show the answer

Throughout the Sprint, as more is learned.

R5How much detail should it have?

Show the answer

Enough that the Developers can inspect their progress in the Daily Scrum.

R6What is the Sprint Goal?

Show the answer

The single objective for the Sprint; a commitment by the Developers that gives coherence and focus and flexibility in the exact work.

R7When is the Sprint Goal created?

Show the answer

In Sprint Planning, and then added to the Sprint Backlog; it must be finalized before the end of Planning.

R8What do the Developers do if the work turns out different from expected?

Show the answer

They collaborate with the Product Owner to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal.

R9Name three attributes of the Sprint Backlog.

Show the answer

A plan by and for the Developers; highly visible and real-time; updated throughout the Sprint; contains the Sprint Goal, selected items and a plan.

R10Give two reasons the Sprint Goal does not change.

Show the answer

It is a commitment; it gives focus and coherence; it is a stable target for inspection; it supports predictability and trust; flexibility sits in the scope.

R11Who may change the Sprint Backlog?

Show the answer

The Developers, who own it; scope is negotiated with the Product Owner.

R12What happens if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete?

Show the answer

The Product Owner may cancel the Sprint.

R13Can Retrospective improvements enter the Sprint Backlog?

Show the answer

Yes, the most impactful ones may be added for the next Sprint.

R14How did the 2017 Guide describe the Sprint Backlog?

Show the answer

As a forecast by the Development Team that included at least one high-priority process improvement from the previous Retrospective.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Sprint Backlog Sprint Goal (why) + selected items (what) + plan (how)
Owner The Developers: "a plan by and for the Developers"
Nature Highly visible, real-time; updated throughout the Sprint
Use Inspected and adapted at the Daily Scrum
Sprint Goal Single objective for the Sprint; commitment; coherence and focus; flexible work
Created In Sprint Planning; finalized before it ends
Changes Plan and scope may change; the Sprint Goal and quality do not
Scope Negotiated between the Developers and the Product Owner
Obsolete goal Product Owner may cancel the Sprint
Retrospective Impactful improvements may enter the next Sprint Backlog
Old wording "Forecast", mandatory process improvement (2017)
